clue.text: They used the last round stone with last of their bricks

parts.note: a cobble is a rounded paving stone

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of each of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Builders finishing a wall with a rounded stone and the last of their bricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last' here is a shoemaker's foot-shaped block, not the final item.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoemakers shape and mend footwear over a last, the wooden foot model of their trade.

clue.text: Warning — with a lot of sparkling wine have some food

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter of the wine goes

parts.note: cava is a Spanish sparkling wine
eat means have some food

explanation.surface: Advice to eat something when drinking lots of fizz.
explanation.definitionFit: A caution or proviso attached to something is a warning.

clue.text: British tree that's thinning out

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: having less hair than before, as the comparative is

parts.note: the alder is a tree of damp ground

explanation.surface: A British tree whose foliage is sparse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone losing hair grows more bare-headed, more so than they were.

clue.text: Anode lost after dissolving iron compound

indicators.note: dissolving breaks something up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An electrode lost in an acid leaves a chemical behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetite, an oxide of iron, is the natural magnet of that name.

clue.text: Sends off for more instruments when college is dismissed

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so the college letter is removed

parts.note: recorders are woodwind instruments

explanation.surface: Ordering more musical instruments after the college orchestra is disbanded.
explanation.definitionFit: Placing another order for further supplies is ordering again.

clue.text: The source of a bit of spam and hock perhaps

definitions.text: The source of a bit of spam and hock perhaps

indicators.note: a bit of here means just the opening letter of the word spam

parts.note: hock is a German white wine, one example of a wine

explanation.surface: Asking where tinned spam and a ham hock come from.
explanation.walkthrough: Hock is both a pig's joint (for the whole clue) and a Rhine wine (for the wordplay).
explanation.definitionFit: Pigs supply the pork in spam and the hock joint, so the animals are their source.

clue.text: A part of reprisal volley?

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a shot belongs to a retaliatory burst of fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'A' alone as the definition, which defines nothing; the whole clue is the definition, as a hidden word that is also a volley.
explanation.definitionFit: A simultaneous discharge of guns, as in a retaliatory barrage, is exactly this.

clue.text: Minister broadcast in periods in between

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A government minister on air during the gaps between programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Temporary periods between one arrangement and the next are stopgap intervals.

clue.text: Fylde in the end behind Orient

indicators.note: in the end picks the final letter of the place name

parts.note: astern means behind, at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A place in Lancashire coming last, behind the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fylde is a coastal plain in Lancashire, England, around Blackpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Orient as an adjective is poetic for oriental, belonging to the East.

clue.text: Tailless rodent is able to settle by old source of vents

indicators.note: tailless means the final letter of the rodent's name is cut off

parts.note: a vole is a small rodent
can means is able

explanation.surface: A small animal settling down beside some ancient feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcanic mountain is where lava, ash and gas are vented, so it is a source of venting.

clue.text: Instruments by delta island show waters down

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so the instruments follow the two letters

parts.note: Delta is D in the NATO phonetic alphabet
lutes are stringed instruments

explanation.surface: Musical instruments by a river delta island appear to weaken something.
explanation.definitionFit: To thin a liquid or weaken an idea is to make it weaker, as with adding water.

clue.text: Fly from Denmark, not Northern Ireland

indicators.note: not means the Northern Ireland letters are left out

parts.note: Danish means from Denmark

explanation.surface: An insect from Denmark that isn't found in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like the insect but is the verb: rush.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly is to rush or hurry away quickly.

clue.text: Not covered, ignored at the outset, like the regions

indicators.note: ignored at the outset means the first letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: bare means not covered
as means like

explanation.surface: Describing regions left uncovered and overlooked from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Regions and zones are synonyms for parts of a territory.

clue.text: Record nothing — sure to become garbled speech

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: garbled means jumbled up, so the letters of sure are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recording of nothing is bound to produce scrambled talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become garbled' turns SURE into URSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal talk or lecture on a subject is a speech.

clue.text: Emergency committee required for venomous snake

definitions.meaning: the UK government's crisis committee, named after Cabinet Office Briefing Room A
a hooded poisonous snake of Africa and Asia

explanation.surface: A crisis meeting called to deal with a dangerous serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: The British crisis committee and the hooded serpent share the same name.

clue.text: Good God! Is it an angry right-winger?

parts.note: Ammon is the Egyptian god also called Amun

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at an angry red-faced political figure.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a pink-faced, angry older conservative is called a gammon, after the colour of cured ham.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses this ham word for a red-faced, ranting conservative.

clue.text: Robot applying gold to upper surface over one portion

indicators.note: in a down answer over means placed above what follows

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
the top is the upper surface
I is the Roman numeral one
a lot is a portion, as at auction

explanation.surface: A robot gilding the top of something above a section.
explanation.definitionFit: An automatic pilot is a machine that flies a plane without human control, a kind of robot.

clue.text: One looking around in the distance — maybe from crow's nest?

definitions.text: One looking around in the distance — maybe from crow's nest?

indicators.note: around means the seer word goes round the distance word

parts.note: a seer is one who sees
afar means in the distance

explanation.surface: A lookout scanning the horizon from the crow's nest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor might keep watch from the crow's nest, the lookout high on a ship's mast.

clue.text: Tory battle is in the soup

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, a Tory
the Somme was a First World War battle

explanation.surface: A Conservative fight has landed someone in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' suggests being in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear broth served as a starter is a type of soup.

clue.text: Nice boy in school's new addition for cricket team

indicators.note: addition means the following letter is tacked on to the end

parts.note: in Nice, France, a schoolboy or pupil is an élève

explanation.surface: A pleasant schoolboy joins the cricket side as a new member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, so the boy in school is French: ELEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket side fields this number of players, so it is used as a name for the team.

clue.text: Earth and two trees — this is soothing sight

definitions.note: read as a noun phrase: something that soothes the eyes

parts.note: yew and ash are two trees; the pair supplies both tree names in turn
the second of the two trees is the ash

explanation.surface: A view of earth and a pair of trees as a calming scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotion bathing the eyes soothes them, so it soothes the organs of vision.

clue.text: The second person there before absconding is a teenager

parts.note: you is the second-person pronoun

indicators.note: absconding means running off, so the word for before leaves the word there

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone who was there earlier has run off, and it's a teenager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absconding' takes ERE out of THERE, leaving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Youth can mean a young person, an adolescent between childhood and adulthood.

clue.text: In one short day starter in office is to show a lot of cheek

definitions.text: to show a lot of cheek

indicators.note: in means the office letter goes inside the day abbreviation

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday

indicators.note: starter in takes the opening letter of office

explanation.surface: A newcomer at work being very cheeky on their first day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheek' here is a buttock, not impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: To bare one's buttocks as a prank is to expose a lot of cheek.

clue.text: Theologian in the papers for fraud

indicators.note: in means the theologian letters go inside the papers word

parts.note: a file is a collection of papers
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian

explanation.surface: A theologian in the newspapers over a scam.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle or racket is a fraud.

clue.text: They say river to the underworld doesn't twist

indicators.note: they say means the answer is what is heard when the river is named

parts.note: the Styx is the river leading to Hades in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A legend that the river of the dead doesn't wind.
explanation.walkthrough: In card games such as pontoon a player either twists (takes a card) or sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: In pontoon, standing on one's hand rather than taking another card is the opposite of twisting.

clue.text: In Fresno I suffer, holding such outpourings back

indicators.note: back means the hidden letters read in reverse
holding means the words contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: Someone in Fresno complaining about their suffering, keeping their outpourings in.
explanation.definitionFit: Gushing outflows of feeling or words are outpourings.

clue.text: Polish joint of beef brought to Spain

parts.note: shin is a cut of beef
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A Polish cut of beef imported into Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish something is to buff it to a gleam.

clue.text: Roger soaked in beer makes an impression

indicators.note: soaked in means the letter sits within the beer word

parts.note: a pint is a measure of beer
R is radio code for roger, received

explanation.surface: Someone called Roger, drunk on beer, makes a big impression.
explanation.walkthrough: In radio talk 'Roger' means message received, and R stands for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed copy or mark is an impression, as in a print of an engraving.

clue.text: Maybe between 1820 and 1830 reportedly put on trial

indicators.note: reportedly means the answer sounds like the phrase given

parts.note: George IV reigned from 1820 to 1830, so that span is an example of a reign

explanation.surface: Someone being tried for something done in the 1820s.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring someone before a court to answer a charge is to try them.

clue.text: Like air I'm cold when blown with energy

indicators.note: blown means scattered about, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone shivering in a wind and needing energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' is a tune, not the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune, and something tuneful is like one.

clue.text: Sounds husky, what has croup in the end?

definitions.text: what has croup in the end

indicators.note: sounds means the answer is said like the word for husky

parts.note: hoarse means husky in voice

explanation.surface: A husky-voiced patient, as though suffering from croup.
explanation.walkthrough: Croup is a children's cough, but also the rump of this animal, its back end.
explanation.definitionFit: The croup is the rump of a mount, at its rear end.

clue.text: Possibly down here and fast moving

indicators.note: moving means the letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Something feeling low and fast-moving around here.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is soft plumage, an example of the covering of birds.
